forces.title: Geopolitical conflict and chokepoint closures disrupt LPG supply chain
forces.description: Geopolitical conflicts in West Asia and the closure of strategic shipping routes like the Strait of Hormuz have severely disrupted India's LPG supply chain. This led to a significant increase in LPG sourcing costs and under-recoveries for OMCs in Q1FY27, necessitating costly diversification to alternative suppliers (e.g., the US) and government compensation. Despite a projected fall in under-recoveries in Q2FY27, the structural vulnerability to international price volatility and import dependency remains high, impacting OMC profitability and consumer prices.
forces.source_title: OMCs LPG Under Recovery Expected to Fall ~40% Q-o-Q in Q2FY27

forces.title: Threat of US tariffs on Russian oil buyers impacts India's crude strategy
forces.description: The proposed US Graham Act, authorizing up to 100% tariffs on top buyers of Russian oil (including India), poses a significant geopolitical risk. While the direct financial benefit of Russian crude discounts has largely eroded to ~$2-4/bbl, a forced, disorderly exit from Russian sourcing could tighten global crude supply, especially if chokepoints like Hormuz remain closed. This would push Brent prices significantly higher, inflicting more material damage on the Indian economy than the direct tariff impact, challenging India's policy agility in crude procurement and trade relations.
forces.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

forces.title: Rising Brent crude prices above $100/bbl threaten OMCs' profitability
forces.description: A sustained increase in Brent crude prices above $100/bbl is a critical monitorable for India's oil economy. While OMCs currently have a ~$27-29/bbl headroom against a breakeven of ~$115/bbl, a significant and rapid rise beyond this threshold would erode that buffer quickly. This would force the government to implement further policy measures, such as additional excise duty cuts (impacting fiscal health) or sharper retail price hikes (leading to consumer inflation and demand destruction), putting substantial stress on OMC margins and overall macroeconomic stability.
forces.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

forces.title: India's LPG import sourcing structurally shifting towards diversification
forces.description: India, historically dependent on West Asian countries for ~90% of its LPG imports (which comprise ~60% of total LPG requirement), has undergone a structural shift due to geopolitical disruptions. Following the Strait of Hormuz closure, India rapidly diversified sourcing to the United States and other alternative markets. This strategic pivot, initially driven by emergency, is now expected to be sustained. Even after Middle East supplies normalize, the US is expected to retain a significant share of India's LPG import portfolio, as OMCs prioritize supply diversification and energy security, albeit at higher landed costs.
forces.source_title: OMCs LPG Under Recovery Expected to Fall ~40% Q-o-Q in Q2FY27

forces.title: Ethanol program evolving to transport energy backbone for sovereignty
forces.description: India's ethanol blending program has evolved from a policy intervention to address sugar surplus and reduce crude import dependence into a strategic lever. With E20 blending achieved ahead of schedule, ethanol is transitioning from a blending component to a potential 'transport energy backbone.' This shift aims to structurally reduce exposure to global crude price volatility and achieve energy sovereignty, where domestic cost structures play a larger role in determining retail prices. This requires moving beyond 1G feedstocks, diversifying demand pathways, and aligning infrastructure and vehicle ecosystems.
forces.source_title: Beyond E20: Repositioning ethanol as India's transport energy backbone

forces.title: Stakeholder misalignment hinders ethanol program expansion beyond E20
forces.description: The successful scaling of ethanol blending to E20 masks significant structural misalignments among key stakeholders, limiting further expansion. Ethanol producers, having scaled capacity under assured demand, now face underutilization risk. OMCs are cautious about incremental capital expenditure for multi-grade systems. OEMs hesitate to scale flex-fuel vehicles without clear demand visibility and economic incentives for consumers. This fragmented progress means individual stakeholder readiness isn't translating into system-wide scale, hindering the program's ability to evolve beyond the E20 ceiling, impacting producers, OMCs, and vehicle manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Beyond E20: Repositioning ethanol as India's transport energy backbone

forces.title: Limitations of 1G feedstock and pricing rigidity for ethanol beyond E20
forces.description: Scaling ethanol beyond E20 faces significant constraints from its current reliance on 1G feedstocks (sugarcane, food grains) due to competing uses ('food-versus-fuel' concerns) and high-water intensity (e.g., ~2,860 litres of water per litre of ethanol from sugarcane). Additionally, the administered, cost-based pricing framework for ethanol lacks market responsiveness, leading to a disconnect with global crude prices. This rigidity and the structural limitations of 1G pathways make further large-scale expansion increasingly complex and less cost-competitive, hindering India's ambition for ethanol to become a core transport fuel.
forces.source_title: Beyond E20: Repositioning ethanol as India's transport energy backbone

forces.title: Inadequate fuel distribution infrastructure for multi-grade ethanol blends
forces.description: The current fuel distribution infrastructure, designed for a centrally blended, uniform E20 product, poses a significant bottleneck for transitioning to higher ethanol blends (E85, E100). A multi-grade fuel system requires extensive upgrades across storage, transport, and dispensing equipment at approximately 100,000 fuel stations nationwide. This introduces new logistical complexities and demands substantial capital expenditure. Without these infrastructure enhancements, the ability to store and deliver diverse ethanol-petrol blends simultaneously remains limited, hindering consumer adoption and the overall expansion of the ethanol program.
forces.source_title: Beyond E20: Repositioning ethanol as India's transport energy backbone

forces.title: Structural dependence on imported LNG for fertilizer production creates vulnerability
forces.description: India's fertilizer system carries a high structural exposure to external energy shocks due to its significant dependence on imported LNG. Approximately 50% of LNG demand is met through imports, heavily concentrated in the Gulf and reliant on chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz. Ammonia production, critical for nitrogenous fertilizers like urea, relies on hydrogen derived from natural gas. Disruptions in LNG supply, as seen with the Hormuz closure, immediately cascade into increased feedstock costs, price volatility, and supply risks for fertilizers, impacting agricultural productivity and food security.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: Significant government investment plans for upstream oil and gas
forces.description: The Indian government has unveiled substantial investment plans for the upstream oil and gas sector, including US$348-406 billion by 2035 and a specific US$67 billion for the gas sector over the next 5-6 years. These investments aim to enhance energy security, double natural gas production to 60 BCM, and increase gas's share in the primary energy mix from 6% to 15%. This strategic capital injection provides a strong tailwind for upstream E&P companies, driving exploration and development activities, and boosting domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.
forces.source_title: Oil And Gas Industry In India

forces.title: Government support and demand drive LNG import capacity expansion
forces.description: India's growing energy demand and strategic objective to increase natural gas's share in the energy mix are strong tailwinds for LNG. As the world's fourth-largest LNG importer, India plans to significantly expand its LNG import capacity to 50 MT in the coming years. This expansion is backed by substantial investments in gas infrastructure, including pipelines and LNG stations, and supportive policies for city gas distribution (CGD). This fuels demand for LNG import facilities and reinforces India's role in global LNG trade, ensuring energy availability for various sectors.
forces.source_title: Oil And Gas Industry In India

forces.title: Ambitious refining capacity expansion plans driven by surging oil demand
forces.description: India's refining sector is experiencing strong tailwinds from surging domestic oil demand, positioning it as the world's third-largest oil consumer. The country plans to double its refining capacity from 258.12 MMTPA (FY25) to 450-500 MMTPA by 2030, with a long-term target of 667 MTPA by 2040. This massive expansion, including adding 1 million barrels per day by 2028, is crucial to meet projected oil demand growth (2x to 11 mbpd by 2045) and support India's ambition to become a petrochemicals powerhouse. This drives substantial capital expenditure and opportunities for refiners and associated industries.
forces.source_title: Oil And Gas Industry In India

forces.title: Government initiatives expanding city gas distribution and alternative fuels
forces.description: Government policies and initiatives are significantly boosting the gas distribution sector. The PNGRB is working to expand city gas distribution (CGD) networks, targeting 126.3 million PNG connections and 18,336 CNG stations by 2034. Additionally, city gas companies plan to add 50 new LNG stations and expand compressed biogas (CBG) infrastructure. This robust governmental and private sector push, coupled with increasing CNG vehicle registrations and rising gas sales, creates a strong tailwind for CGD companies, driving increased demand for natural gas in transport, residential, and industrial applications.
forces.source_title: Oil And Gas Industry In India

forces.title: Government support for 2G bioethanol projects under PM JI-VAN Yojana
forces.description: The Indian government is actively promoting the development of Second Generation (2G) bioethanol projects through the amended PM JI-VAN Yojana. This scheme provides significant financial support, with over US$106.7 million (Rs. 908 crore) already approved for various commercial-scale 2G bioethanol initiatives. This commitment is a strong tailwind for the bioenergy sector, encouraging the use of agricultural residues and other non-food feedstocks, thereby diversifying the ethanol supply base, reducing reliance on 1G sources, and contributing to India's clean energy goals and energy security.

forces.title: AI adoption for efficiency and productivity across energy sector operations
forces.description: The energy sector is rapidly integrating AI solutions, moving from pilots to wider enterprise deployment, particularly in oil & gas and power & utilities. AI is driving efficiency in operations (e.g., faster exploration, production optimization of wells/mines) and productivity in processes (e.g., smart grid management, predictive maintenance). This extends to back-office functions like finance and procurement. The IT function is increasingly leading AI strategy (58% of organizations), reflecting a shift towards deeper technical accountability and integration within core business systems, transforming how energy organizations operate and create value.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Energy, Natural Resources and Chemicals

viewpoints.title: OMCs face sustained LPG under-recovery pressure despite expected Q2FY27 moderation
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings notes that despite an anticipated ~40% q-o-q fall in LPG under-recoveries in Q2FY27 due to declining Saudi CP prices, the overall burden on OMCs remains significant. Geopolitical disruptions in West Asia, leading to higher sourcing costs and supply diversification, caused substantial losses in Q1FY27. While government compensation provides some relief, the cumulative under-recovery burden will likely keep LPG profitability under pressure in the near term, highlighting ongoing vulnerability to international market volatility and domestic pricing regulations.
viewpoints.source_title: OMCs LPG Under Recovery Expected to Fall ~40% Q-o-Q in Q2FY27

viewpoints.title: Indian refiners demonstrate agility in crude sourcing, but new disruptions pose risk
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings acknowledges Indian refiners' proven agility in redirecting crude supply, citing the rapid shift from Iraqi and Saudi grades to Russian barrels during the Strait of Hormuz closure in 2026. However, it warns that the sector's resilience is untested against a 'different kind of disruption'—specifically, a tariff-driven constraint on Russian purchases combined with a closed chokepoint. This dual threat could tighten global crude supply significantly and inflict material damage on the Indian economy, calling for close monitoring through 2026.
viewpoints.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

viewpoints.title: US Graham Act is tail risk; sustained Brent above $100/bbl is core threat
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings considers the US Graham Act (proposing tariffs on Russian oil buyers) a 'credible tail risk' rather than the 'central threat' to India's oil economy. The benefit of discounted Russian crude has largely eroded, and India's diversified sourcing base can absorb supply constraints. The far greater challenge, they argue, is a sustained movement of Brent crude above $100/bbl, especially if combined with chokepoint closures. Such a scenario would inflict more material damage than the erosion of Russian discounts, necessitating further policy measures.
viewpoints.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

viewpoints.title: Energy sector making solid progress leveraging technology for value creation
viewpoints.description: KPMG notes that the energy sector is decisively integrating technology, moving beyond pilots to achieve clearer financial value. Investment levels are steady, with many organizations reporting returns from production optimization, predictive maintenance, and integrated asset management. The sector prioritizes integrated digital ecosystems supported by cloud platforms, digital twins, automation, and AI-driven decision support. While scaling AI solutions remains a challenge, there's an exciting path ahead to convert technology investments into sustained operational performance and growing financial returns across oil and gas, power, utilities, mining, chemicals, and renewables.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Energy, Natural Resources and Chemicals

viewpoints.title: IT function is ideally positioned to drive enterprise-wide AI strategy
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India believes the IT function is best suited to lead AI strategy, providing a holistic view across all functions and an enterprise-wide development platform. This approach brings structure to AI ambitions and a scalable delivery method, preventing fragmented point solutions. IT can also effectively manage relationships with solution providers, crucial for successful collaborative models. Energy organizations acknowledge this, with 58% reporting that IT now leads AI strategy, reflecting a move towards deeper technical accountability and higher integration of AI within core business systems.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Energy, Natural Resources and Chemicals

viewpoints.title: Ethanol program enters new phase, repositioning as transport energy backbone
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India asserts that India’s ethanol program is at a strategic inflection point, having achieved E20 blending ahead of schedule. The focus is shifting from merely blending ethanol to repositioning it as a 'transport energy backbone' to moderate crude price volatility and strengthen resilience. The next phase requires a structural shift beyond 1G feedstocks, diversified demand pathways, and alignment of infrastructure, pricing, and vehicle ecosystems for flexible utilization. This transition aims for energy sovereignty, where domestic cost structures play a larger role in determining retail fuel prices.
viewpoints.source_title: Beyond E20: Repositioning ethanol as India's transport energy backbone

viewpoints.title: India must proactively manage energy vulnerability amid West Asian volatility
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings highlights India's acute economic exposure to the 'stop-start' US-Iran conflict, which causes volatile crude prices, LNG supply squeezes, and macroeconomic instability. While crude sourcing is diversified, natural gas dependence on West Asia (50% imports through Hormuz) remains a vulnerability. India must focus on reducing imported oil/gas share by developing alternative domestic sources like syngas from coal gasification and nuclear energy, and by building strategic petroleum reserves. Policy agility is crucial for transforming this geopolitical crisis into a test of macroeconomic resilience.
